title: One-Pan Chicken Dumplings (Wonton-Wrapper 'Pot Pie')
summary: A pork-free one-pan 'pot pie' shortcut: seasoned ground-chicken dumpling filling is seared in a pan, capped with wonton wrappers, steamed in chicken broth, then finished with a soy-black-vinegar dipping sauce, chili oil, green onions and sesame seeds. The description gives a measured recipe; the narration adds two extra filling ingredients (honey, white pepper) and conflicts with the description on chicken form and chili-oil placement — all preserved, not reconciled.

ingredients.note: CONFLICT: the description lists '1lb chicken breast', but the narration says 'ground chicken' and the frames show raw ground/minced chicken in the bowl. Whether the creator ground the breast or used pre-ground chicken is not stated; both surfaces preserved.
This is the filling's 1 tbsp soy sauce; the dipping sauce separately uses 1/4 cup.
Filling allocation; the dipping sauce separately uses 2 tsp.
Source says 'Green onions chopped' with no quantity; also used as a garnish.

PLACEMENT CONFLICT: the description lists 2 tsp chili oil among the main ingredients (implying it goes in the filling) but its own method step 6 says 'Garnish with sauce, chili oil...' — i.e. drizzled on at the end. The narration also puts chili oil in the filling mix. Use is split across the two surfaces; not reconciled.
NARRATION-ONLY: 'a little bit of honey' is added to the filling in the video but does NOT appear in the description ingredient list. No quantity given ('a little bit').
NARRATION-ONLY: 'some white pepper' is added to the filling in the video but does NOT appear in the description ingredient list. No quantity given.

steps.text: Combine the ground chicken with the green onion, ginger, garlic, soy sauce and sesame oil — the narration also adds chili oil, a little honey and some white pepper at this stage.

ingredients.note: No count given; enough to cap each filling mound.
Description says 'chicken broth'; the narration says 'chicken stock'. Wording drift preserved; existing chicken-stock filter key reused.

steps.text: Scoop dumpling-sized balls of the filling onto the pan and sear.
Cover each seared mound with a wonton wrapper.
Add the chicken broth and steam. TIME CONFLICT: the description says steam 10–15 minutes until cooked; the narration says 15 minutes. Both recorded.
Combine the soy sauce, black vinegar and sesame oil for the dipping sauce. The video only says 'Sauce.' over this beat; no mixing method or heating is specified.

ingredients.note: Listed in the description ingredients and as a garnish in step 6; narration does not mention them. No quantity.
Reserved from the chopped green onions; garnish quantity not separately stated.

steps.text: Garnish the finished dumplings with the dipping sauce, chili oil, green onions and sesame seeds.

notes: Source is split: the 30-second narration is the cooking demo; the description carries the measured ingredient list and method. They disagree in several places, and every disagreement is preserved rather than repaired.

CHICKEN FORM: description says '1lb chicken breast'; narration says 'ground chicken' and the frames confirm raw ground/minced chicken. Recorded as both; the creator never says whether the breast was ground down.

EXTRA FILLING INGREDIENTS: the narration adds honey and white pepper to the filling; neither appears in the description list. Added as rows named from the narration with basis 'unstated' and null amounts ('a little bit' / 'some' are vague, i.e. no quantity).
CHILI OIL PLACEMENT: the description's ingredient list implies 2 tsp chili oil in the filling, but its own step 6 and the garnish use put chili oil on at the end. Both placements retained.
STEAM TIME: description 10–15 minutes; narration 15 minutes. Both recorded; do not pick one.
BROTH vs STOCK wording drift (description 'chicken broth', narration 'chicken stock') preserved; same liquid, one 1/4 cup amount.
Sesame seeds appear only in the description (ingredients + step 6), not the narration. Green onions are used in both the filling and the garnish.

Vision read (control-proven) of frames at 5/8/13/21 s confirmed: ground/minced chicken, oil poured over garlic/green-onion/chili on the meat, a lifted scoop of mixed filling, and dumplings steaming in a shallow liquid pool; NO readable on-screen text anywhere. tesseract over 11 frames returned only noise.
Capture-time metrics (3,205,186 views / 98,806 likes / 990 comments) are platform snapshots, not reach or conversion evidence.

Creator hook is a substitution/pork-free framing ('if you can't eat pork but want one pan easy chicken dumplings') and a pot-pie comparison ('Who needs a pot pie when you've got THIS?'); both are creator claims.
gaps: Yield/dumpling count is unstated, so wonton-wrapper count and per-pan batch size cannot be derived.
Chicken form is unresolved: 'chicken breast' (description) vs 'ground chicken' (narration + frames). No instruction to grind is given.
Honey and white pepper quantities are unstated ('a little bit', 'some').
Green onion, sesame seed and garnish-green-onion quantities are unstated.
Chili-oil placement (filling vs garnish) is contradictory across the description's own surfaces; final location is unresolved.
Steam time is 10–15 minutes (description) or 15 minutes (narration); the exact target and the doneness cue beyond 'until cooked' are unstated.
Sear heat/temperature, pan size, oil for searing and the sauce's mixing/heating method are unstated.
Internal doneness temperature for the chicken is not given.
No nutrition information is provided on any surface.

source.evidence: Public description (measured ingredient list + 6-step method), YouTube transcript-API (17 English auto-generated segments, is_generated=true), public oEmbed, sanitized extractor metadata, ffprobe receipt, and 11 sampled frames: tesseract sweep (noise only) plus one control-proven auxiliary-vision read confirming ground chicken, the oil-pour, the filling scoop, steaming dumplings and no on-screen text. Master video not retained; SHA-256 and re-fetch command kept in the vault evidence bundle.
source.quantity_basis: Quantities come from the creator's description; the narration supplies two additional filling ingredients (honey, white pepper) with no amounts. Where the two sources conflict (chicken form, chili-oil placement, steam time, broth/stock wording), both readings are recorded and none is silently chosen. No amounts, temperatures or times were invented from generic cooking knowledge; vague narration ('a little bit', 'some') is treated as unstated.
